newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher as USDA cuts wheat stocks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher as USDA cuts wheat stocks.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on a cut by USDA in its estimate for world and U.S. ending stocks, traders said.
"World ending stocks were cut, U.S. stocks were cut and that prompted some to cover their shorts," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.

USDA in its November production and supply/demand reports Tuesday trimmed to 435 million bushels from the previous 470 million, its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. wheat ending stocks. The 1996-97 U.S. marketing year is slated to end on May 31.
USDA also cut its outlook for world wheat supplies.
The world ending stocks tally was trimmed to 110.79 million tonnes from 116.53 million tonnes predicted by the government in its October report.
USDA noted that its world wheat output estimate fell from last month, largely due to a drop in India's crop.
Wheat futures also found support on a recent firmer tone for wheat prices in countries other than the United States.
"The wheat market is stabilizing worldwide," Searcy said.
CBOT wheat closed four to 8-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with December up eight at $3.91-1/2. March was up 8-3/4 at $3.87-3/4 a bushel.
Wheat futures also found follow-through support from recent talk that Turkey soon may be in the market for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

The Turkish Grain Board (TMO), the state agency that buys grain from farmers, will step into the market by selling wheat to local millers to curb rising bread prices, but it still needs to import an unspecified amount of wheat soon, Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said Tuesday. Demirci said last week the TMO could import up to 500,000 tonnes of wheat through a tender. A grain official told Reuters the tender would be held "as soon as possible for an unspecified amount."
Fund buying led the way up with ING Derivatives, Dean Witter Reynolds and Iowa Grain each purchasing 1.5 million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts above the 13,779 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Continental Grain sold 150 March $3.60 puts at six cents and Tenco Inc bought 100 March $3.90 calls at 13-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, below the 7,944 traded Monday.
Technicians eyed the ability of December to break above first resistance at $3.87-1/2 and set a session high of $3.96 just below second resistance at $3.96-1/2.

The daily relative strength index (RSI) for December moved into neutral territory on a short term basis closing at 56.3 points. Technicians generally consider an RSI of 30 or less as an oversold market and 70 or more as oversold. (c) Reuters Limited 1996
